First off, welcome to gun ownership! One of the first things you'll get to witness first hand is just how friendly most gun owners are when engaged in the sport. If I were you, I'd go to your nicest local range with $100 in your pocket. Pay for a gun safety class if they offer one. (Almost all ranges offer one) Then rent a couple of guns and talk to the people who are also using the range. Everyone is friendly and you'll probably be invited to learn about and fire the guns that people have brought with them. For this $100 you'll get a good understanding of the basics of gun safety, a chance to shoot at least a couple different guns and you'll probably meet some cool people.

Now for a list of what I think is cool/viable for someone just starting out.

You must at some point own a Ruger 10/22 rifle.

If you want something for home defense then buy a Mossberg 500 or Remington 870 in 12 gauge

If you live out West and will have lots of opportunities to shoot outside on private or public land, you're going to get a lot of use out of an AR15. Rock River Arms and Wyndham Weaponry make great guns, but there are probably more than a thousand manufacturers at this point and few of them are truly bad.

Pistols can be frustrating for new shooters because they require more skill to shoot at a very basic level than rifles and shotguns. That being said, a Glock 19 does everything in a relatively inexpensive and very comfortable package.

Final thought, don't worry so much about how much a gun costs because you'll spend way more than that over the life of the firearm in ammunition costs if you really get into the sport and shoot consistently. A $1,000 Sig Sauer and a $550 Glock cost $2,200 and $1,750 respectively after 5 years of shooting a hundred rounds of the cheapest 9mm per month. If you consider the cost of running self defense ammo through the gun to train and rotate for fresh ammo, the percentage difference in price is even smaller. This is of course just the way I look at it and I own both lol.

Everyone is different. Go to your local fun store and hold a few, find what's comfortable. BEFORE you actually go shooting memorize gun safety rules.

A .22 will have the least kick and be dirt cheap to shoot but can be hard to find in done places because demand is high.

Semi auto will have less kick and composite stocks are lighter than wood.

Ultimately, find what is comfortable for you. Some shop/range combos let you rent firearms so you can test different types on the range before you buy.

Look into a gun/hunter safety or CCW course as well, that will teach you safety, good practice, and basics. And remember that the safety rules MUST ALWAYS be followed. Shooting is a ton of fun, but dangerous if you don't follow the rules/do stupid shit.

Good luck and have fun.
